title: Kunneth for cohomology with closed support
statement:
Let $k$ be the algebraically closed field of
[def-weil-finite-field-fiber]. For a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ and an integer $n\geq1$, put
$A=\mathcal O_E/\varpi_E^n$, and let $Z\subset X,W\subset Y$
be closed subschemes of
separated finite-type
$k$-schemes.
Let $K\in D^b(X_{\mathrm{et}},A)$ and
$L\in D^b(Y_{\mathrm{et}},A)$ be
bounded complexes,
with $L$ of
finite Tor amplitude.
Then the supported
exterior product is an isomorphism:

$$
\kappa^{Z,W}_{K,L}:
R\Gamma_Z(X,K)\otimes_A^LR\Gamma_W(Y,L)
\xrightarrow{\ \sim\ }
R\Gamma_{Z\times W}(X\times_kY,K\boxtimes_A^L L).
$$

Here $R\Gamma_Z,R\Gamma_W$ are the
derived support functors.
The assertion also holds for the pro-etale realizations of these
complexes equipped with
etale-origin witnesses.

proof.text: Put $U=X\setminus Z$, $V=Y\setminus W$, $P=X\times_kY$ and $F=p_X^*K\otimes_A^Lp_Y^*L$. We first check the open schemes needed below. A field is Noetherian: its only ideals are $0$ and $(1)$. Thus $\operatorname{Spec}k$ is Noetherian, using the affine definition [pqf-def-locnoeth]. By [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian], $X,Y$ are Noetherian. By [lem-weil-pbc-noetherian-open-subscheme-noetherian], every open subscheme of either is Noetherian and quasi-compact. In particular the intersection of $U$ with every affine open of $X$ is quasi-compact; hence $U\hookrightarrow X$ is quasi-compact, and is finite type by [lem-weil-pbc-qc-open-immersion-finite-type]. Choose a finite affine cover of $X$ and finite affine covers of these intersections. The composite finite-type presentations give a finite affine cover of $U$ by finitely generated $k$-algebras: the generators are those at the two stages together [def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. The same argument applies to $V$. The diagonal of $U/k$ is the base change of the closed diagonal of $X/k$ along $U\times_kU\to X\times_kX$, since a pair of points of $U$ equal in $X$ is equal in $U$. It is closed by [lem-weil-pbc-proper-fp-permanence](b). Thus $U$ is separated by [def-weil-proper-morphism]; likewise $V$.

source.place: Paragraph 1: geometric hypotheses on the open complements; Stacks 01T6, 01OW, 01OZ, 0052, 04ZA, 01T0, 01T2, 01QR

proof.text: The projection $P\to Y$ is separated and finite type by [lem-pod-separated-finite-type-base-change], applied to $X\to\operatorname{Spec}k$ and $Y\to\operatorname{Spec}k$. Its composite with $Y\to\operatorname{Spec}k$ is separated by [lem-weil-pbc-proper-fp-permanence](e). It is finite type directly from [def-weil-finite-type-morphism]: choose finite affine covers of $X,Y$; their products cover $P$ and have coordinate rings $B\otimes_k C$, generated by the finitely many elements $b_i\otimes1$ and $1\otimes c_j$ when $b_i,c_j$ generate $B,C$. This also applies to $U\times Y$, $X\times V$ and $U\times V$, since step 1 established the same hypotheses for $U,V$. Thus every product ambient scheme used in the localization and site-comparison lemmas satisfies their geometric hypotheses.

source.place: Paragraphs 1-4: geometric hypotheses on the products; Stacks 01KU and 01T4

proof.text: Choose $c$ with $H^i(K)=0$ for $i<c$, and $a,b$ bounding the Tor amplitude of $L$. Represent $K$ by its good lower truncation: it is zero below $c$, is $\operatorname{coker}(d^{c-1})$ in degree $c$, and retains the original terms above $c$. The hypothesis on cohomology makes the truncation quasi-isomorphic to $K$. By [lem-kun-0f1m], represent $L$ by a K-flat complex $Q$ of flat terms, zero below $a$, whose termwise module pullbacks remain K-flat with flat terms. For every projection or open immersion $u$ in this proof, [prop-weil-pbc-inverse-image-modules-exact](1)-(3) identifies $u^{-1}A$ with the constant ring sheaf and module pullback with exact inverse image. Consequently $p_X^*K$ still has a representative zero below $c$, and $p_Y^*Q$ is K-flat and zero below $a$. By the K-flat computation of derived tensor [def-kun-derived-tensor], their total tensor represents $F$. In total degree $r<c+a$ there is no pair $i\geq c,j\geq a$ with $i+j=r$, so that term is zero. Exact open restriction gives the identical argument on $U\times Y$, $X\times V$, and $U\times V$. All the exterior-product complexes required below are therefore bounded below. This uses no flatness or constructibility hypothesis on $K$.

source.place: Paragraph 1, sentence 2: boundedness via the lower K-flat representative; Stacks 0F1M

proof.text:
For the support pair $W\subset Y$, [lem-pur-support-restriction-triangle] with $B=Y,C=W$ gives the triangle $R\Gamma_W(Y,L)\to R\Gamma(Y,L)\to R\Gamma(V,L|_V)\to R\Gamma_W(Y,L)[1]$. Tensor it on the left with $R\Gamma(X,K)$; this is distinguished by [lem-pc-derived-tensor-second-factor-functor] with $R=A$, using the symmetric tensor identification. Compare with the support triangle for $X\times W\subset X\times Y$, whose complement is $X\times V$. By [lem-pur-supported-product-localization] in the second variable, the supported product $\kappa^{X,W}_{K,L}$ and the two ordinary exterior products form a morphism of these triangles, including the last square. The ordinary products for $(X,Y)$ and $(X,V)$ are isomorphisms by [lem-pur-ordinary-kunneth-finite-ring], which explicitly states invertibility of the canonical Kunneth arrow in the ordinary unbounded small etale $A$-module derived categories. Our bounded complexes and their open restrictions are objects of those categories, and $\ell\neq\operatorname{char}(k)$ is part of [def-weil-finite-field-fiber]; $V$ is separated of finite type by step 1. Therefore [lem-sf-triangle-morphism-iso] shows that the actual supported product
$$R\Gamma(X,K)\otimes_A^LR\Gamma_W(Y,L)\xrightarrow{\sim}R\Gamma_{X\times W}(X\times Y,F)$$
is an isomorphism. For full support, sections with support are all sections, so $\kappa^{X,Y}$ is the ordinary product by [def-pur-supported-exterior-product].

Perform the preceding construction with $U$ in place of $X$ and $K|_U$ in place of $K$. The open $U$ is a separated finite-type $k$-scheme; the boundedness requirements were verified in steps 1-3. The support triangles [lem-pur-support-restriction-triangle] and the exact tensor functor [lem-pc-derived-tensor-second-factor-functor] therefore apply. The morphism of triangles supplied by [lem-pur-supported-product-localization] has ordinary products on $(U,Y)$ and $(U,V)$ as its second and third components, which are the full-support ordinary products by [def-pur-supported-exterior-product] and are isomorphisms by [lem-pur-ordinary-kunneth-finite-ring]. By [lem-sf-triangle-morphism-iso] its first component is the isomorphism
$$\kappa^{U,W}_{K|_U,L}:R\Gamma(U,K|_U)\otimes_A^LR\Gamma_W(Y,L)\xrightarrow{\sim}R\Gamma_{U\times W}(U\times Y,F|_{U\times Y}).$$
The first components in steps 4 and 5 are the specified exterior products, rather than unspecified completions of two commuting squares.

Now use [lem-pur-support-restriction-triangle] for $(X,B=X,C=Z,K)$ and tensor with $R\Gamma_W(Y,L)$. The resulting row is distinguished by [lem-pc-derived-tensor-second-factor-functor]. The target row is [lem-pur-support-restriction-triangle] for $T=X\times Y$, $B=X\times W$, $C=Z\times Y$. Its first support is $(X\times W)\cap(Z\times Y)=Z\times W$ and its third term is $R\Gamma_{U\times W}(U\times Y,F|_{U\times Y})$; in particular its third ambient scheme is $U\times Y$. Apply [lem-pur-supported-product-localization] in the first variable, with its $B=X,C=Z,D=W$. Its three components are precisely $\kappa^{Z,W}_{K,L}$, $\kappa^{X,W}_{K,L}$ and $\kappa^{U,W}_{K|_U,L}$, with the shift identification at the boundary. The second and third are isomorphisms by steps 4 and 5, so [lem-sf-triangle-morphism-iso] proves that $\kappa^{Z,W}_{K,L}$ is an isomorphism. Its identity as the map in [def-pur-supported-exterior-product] is part of the cited localization compatibility, not an appeal to uniqueness of triangle completion.

For the pro-etale realizations first take the canonical witnesses $(K,1)$ and $(L,1)$. By steps 2-3, the site-comparison lemma [lem-pur-support-site-comparison] applies to $(X,Z,K)$, $(Y,W,L)$ and $(P,Z\times W,F)$. Its specified comparison equality gives
$$\kappa^{Z,W}_{\nu_X^*K,\nu_Y^*L}=(R\Gamma_{Z\times W}(\theta)\circ c^{Z\times W}_{P,F})\circ\kappa^{Z,W}_{K,L}\circ(c^Z_{X,K}\otimes_A^Lc^W_{Y,L})^{-1}.$$
The comparisons $c$ and $\theta$ are isomorphisms by that lemma. Derived tensor preserves isomorphisms in either variable, as every functor does. The etale middle factor is an isomorphism by step 6. Hence the actual pro-etale supported product for the canonical realizations is an isomorphism.

source.place: Paragraph 4: comparison equality for the canonical etale-origin realizations

proof.text:
Let the specified witnesses be $\alpha:
u_X^*K\xrightarrow{\sim}K_p$ and $ eta:
u_Y^*L\xrightarrow{\sim}L_p$ [def-weil-pbc-etale-origin-witness]. The pro-etale product is the adjoint of $	heta^L$ followed by the tensor of the two evaluation counits [def-pur-proetale-supported-exterior-product]. Naturality of these counits and of $	heta^L$ therefore gives
$$\kappa^{Z,W}_{K_p,L_p}\circ(R\Gamma_Z(\alpha)\otimes_A^LR\Gamma_W( eta))=R\Gamma_{Z	imes W}(\alpha oxtimes_A^L eta)\circ\kappa^{Z,W}_{
u_X^*K,
u_Y^*L}.$$
Indeed, before taking the adjoint, the two composites agree by the naturality square for each counit, followed by the naturality square for $	heta^L$; the adjunction bijection preserves this equality. Solving the displayed equality for $\kappa^{Z,W}_{K_p,L_p}$ expresses it as the isomorphism of step 7 composed on each side with isomorphisms. This proves the witness-dependent assertion in the ordinary finite-ring module-sheaf categories.

tool_uses.why: Its exact tensor functor applies directly to D(A), the target category of sections; the unit has no ordinary-module tensor exactness statement (lem-kun-derived-tensor-triangulated is stated for sheaves on a scheme).

Generic lower K-flat representative for a complex with lower Tor amplitude; verifies that the exterior-product complex in the unit localization route is bounded below. This unit has no lower K-flat model statement.

Generic exactness of inverse image for constant-ring module sheaves; ensures projection and open pullbacks preserve the bounded coefficient complexes. This unit has no module inverse-image exactness statement.

The generic affine definition of locally Noetherian schemes checks that Spec of the field k is Noetherian before the existing finite-type and open-subscheme lemmas apply. No special purity route is replaced.
